revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Total sales across BioSyent's Canadian Pharmaceutical, International Pharmaceutical, Legacy/Insecticide and (from March 2026) Oral Health segments.

For BioSyent: FY2025 revenue of C$43.05m was ~86% Canadian Pharmaceutical (led by the FeraMAX iron-supplement franchise), before the Oral Science acquisition added a full new Oral Health segment that was already 33% of H1-2026 sales. The March 2026 deal is why the YoY line spikes: Q2-2026 revenue is +95% YoY, the first full quarter including Oral Science.

What to watch:

  • Whether Canadian Pharmaceutical (still ~65% of H1-2026 sales) keeps growing organically once the acquisition annualizes out of the YoY comparison in 2027
  • Whether Oral Science sustains its run-rate or proves ex-growth, as the bear case in the DCF assumes
  • International sales (FeraMAX + Tibelia exports), which grew 302% in FY2025 off a small base but are exposed to Middle East distribution-partner disruption

marginCompression.title: Gross Margin vs. Operating Margin
marginCompression.content:
Gross margin = gross profit / revenue; operating margin = operating income / revenue. BioSyent's asset-light in-licensing model -- it pays for marketing rights to already-approved products rather than developing or manufacturing them -- has historically produced 77-82% gross margins because there is little R&D or manufacturing cost to carry.

For BioSyent: gross margin ran 76.6%-81.9% every year from FY2015 to FY2025. It stepped down to 71.5% in H1-2026 (and operating margin from 26.2% to 21.0%) purely because Oral Science's dental-distribution business carries a structurally lower margin than legacy Pharma -- this is a permanent mix-shift, not a one-off cost.

What to watch:

  • Whether the blended margin stabilizes near the new ~71%/21% level (the DCF's base case assumes gross margin holds near there with EBITDA margin around 25-26%) or drifts further as Oral Health scales
  • Whether cross-selling synergies between the two sales forces claw margin back toward the DCF's 28% EBITDA bull case
  • Increasing competitive activity in the core Canadian oral-iron category, which management itself has flagged as a risk to the higher-margin Pharma engine

fcf.title: Net Income vs. Free Cash Flow
fcf.content:
Free cash flow here is operating cash flow less capital expenditure, as reported. It differs from the DCF's "owner FCF", which additionally deducts stock-based compensation and IFRS-16 lease principal.

For BioSyent: FY2025 owner FCF (DCF basis) was C$7.80m, 1.8x the FY2019-25 median of ~C$4.3m -- a peak year the DCF deliberately does not extrapolate forward, instead building Year-1 FCF from normalized revenue and margin components.

What to watch:

  • Negative quarterly FCF prints, which are normal here (working-capital and tax-payment timing around a small revenue base) rather than a distress signal
  • Whether reinvestment normalizes toward the DCF's assumed 2% of revenue -- FY2025's capex of just C$0.39m understates typical spend (FY2024 spent C$4.6-4.7m on product-rights purchases)
  • Cash conversion once the acquisition-related term loan and revolver are repaid (scheduled by September 2026)

cashDebt.title: Cash vs. Total Debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash and equivalents against total debt on the balance sheet, both from the reported financial statements.

For BioSyent: the company ran debt-free with a growing net-cash cushion for essentially its entire public history -- cash plus short/long-term investments peaked near C$31.9m at December 2025. The March 2026 Oral Science acquisition (C$31.48m total consideration including a C$3.85m contingent-consideration liability) was funded with C$16.3m of BioSyent's own cash plus a new C$6.0m RBC term loan and a C$2.0m revolving-credit draw, pulling combined cash and investments down to C$12.2m by June 2026 -- the first time in recent history the company carries meaningful debt.

What to watch:

  • Repayment of the remaining C$2.0m bank facility, due September 30, 2026, against a maximum funded-debt-to-EBITDA covenant of 2.50x
  • The C$3.85m contingent-consideration liability (Oral Science earn-out/royalty through 2033, capped at C$6.0m), which is debt-like but sits off this chart's TotalDebt column
  • Whether the cash cushion is rebuilt enough to fund further bolt-on M&A, historically a core part of the growth story

buyback.title: Shares Outstanding
buyback.content:
Total common shares outstanding at each period end.

For BioSyent: an active NCIB buyback retired 3.4m shares (~30% of the current count) since December 2018 for roughly C$26.5m at an average C$7.91/share, shrinking the count from 14.51m (FY2018) to 11.26m (FY2025). That trend reversed in March 2026 when 234,192 shares were issued as partial consideration for the Oral Science acquisition, ticking the count back up to 11.39m -- the DCF holds this flat for all ten projection years rather than assuming further shrinkage.

What to watch:

  • Whether NCIB buybacks resume at their historical pace once the acquisition debt is repaid (H1-2026 buyback spend was already stepped up 14x to C$3.09m alongside debt repayment)
  • Further consideration-share issuance tied to the Oral Science earn-out through 2033

dividend.title: Dividend per Share
dividend.content:
Total common-share dividends declared per share for the fiscal year.

For BioSyent: the dividend was introduced in 2022 and has been raised twice since, most recently from C$0.05 to C$0.055 quarterly (+10%) effective the March 2026 payment -- a ~1.4% yield at the current price. Management reiterated the Q3-2026 dividend at C$0.055/share alongside its Q2-2026 results, continuing to pay it out of modelled cash flow even as the company took on its first debt.

What to watch:

  • Whether the payout is maintained through the acquisition-debt repayment period
  • The dividend is modelled as paid out of, not additive to, the DCF's owner free cash flow

ebitda.title: EBITDA & EBITDA Margin
ebitda.content:
Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization, and that figure as a percentage of revenue.

For BioSyent: EBITDA margin sat in the mid-to-high 20s for most of the last decade. Management's own commentary on Q2-2026 results highlighted combined Pharmaceutical and Oral Health growth driving 95% sales growth alongside 80% EBITDA growth -- EBITDA is growing, but slower than revenue, which is the same margin-mix story visible in the gross/operating margin chart.

What to watch:

  • Whether the blended EBITDA margin stabilizes near the DCF base case's ~25-26% (versus ~28% pre-deal) or recovers toward the bull case's 28% via integration synergies
  • Increased H2-2026 selling and marketing spend management has guided ahead of the Thyconvi (liquid levothyroxine) launch, which will pressure near-term EBITDA margin

netMargin.title: Net Margin
netMargin.content:
Net income after tax as a percentage of revenue.

For BioSyent: net margin ran 20-29% through FY2015-2025 but fell to 14% in Q2-2026 (from 20% a year earlier) as Oral Health's lower margin profile and C$0.75m of incremental acquisition-related intangible amortization flowed through. H1-2026 net income was still up 19.7% YoY -- growth continued, just at a materially diluted rate versus the 59.7% revenue growth.

What to watch:

  • Whether amortization of the acquired Oral Science intangibles (72.7% of the provisional purchase-price allocation is intangibles and goodwill) continues to compress reported net margin even as cash EBITDA holds up
  • Any impairment of that intangible/goodwill balance if Oral Science underperforms, which the DCF's bear case explicitly prices in

sbc.title: Stock-Based Compensation
sbc.content:
Non-cash share-based payment expense recognized in the period.

For BioSyent: SBC is small relative to revenue (1.1-1.5%, C$0.625m in FY2025) -- this is not a heavily-dilutive tech-style compensation structure. The DCF expenses it fully in the cash-flow build and holds the share count flat rather than adding a separate dilution adjustment, since double-counting both would overstate the dilution cost.

What to watch:

  • SBC staying in the ~1% of revenue range the DCF projects across all ten years
  • Whether option exercises meaningfully widen the gap between the 11.39m basic count used here and the ~11.5m diluted count
